newsitem.title: ISRAEL: RESEARCH ALERT-Orbotech lowered to buy.
newsitem.headline: RESEARCH ALERT-Orbotech lowered to buy.

text.p: Salomon Brothers on Thursday downgraded Israel's Orbotech Ltd, a maker of automated optical inspection (AOI) systems, to a buy from a strong buy, though it said the company may exceed its 1997 and 1998 profit estimates.

"Although we believe that Orbotrech will continue to exceed our expectations in the coming period, future stock price performance may not justify (a) strong-buy recommendation," analyst Victor Halpert said in a report.

Halpert noted that Orbotech's share price had risen 150 percent in the last seven months to as high as $32, the top of Salomon's 12-month target price range. Orbotech closed in Nasdaq trading on Wednesday at $30.50.

Halpert said Orbtoech continued to register strong sales from its core business of AOI equipment for the printed circuit board (PCB) industry. He said revenues from the company's flat panel display (FPD) AOI business would grow 350 percent this year to about $12 million.
In 1998, the company's new line of shadow mask inspection equipment will post revenues growth to $10 million from a projected $3 million this year, he added.

"Recent announcements regarding new contracts in the PCB and FPD segments boosted our confidence of a potential upside to our 1997 and 1998 (earnings per share) estimates, which currently amount to $1.96 and $2.28, respectively," Halpert said.
